# PyTorch

`torch==2.11.0`. The only machine-learning dependency in the entire source set, and it appears in
exactly one repository: `IT Applications in Business and Commerce`, where it trains the PPO race
driver described in [[proximal-policy-optimisation]] and [[residual-reinforcement-learning]].

Everything else in the corpus that touches numerics uses numpy, and there is no TensorFlow, JAX,
scikit-learn, Stable-Baselines3 or Gymnasium anywhere. **The PPO implementation is hand-written on
top of raw `torch.nn`** — no RL library was used.

## What is actually built with it

Both agent trees define an `ActorCriticNet(nn.Module)`:

- two 256-unit `Tanh` MLP trunks — **separate** `self.actor` and `self.critic`, not a shared
  backbone
- linear `policy_head` and `value_head` on top
- a learned `log_std` as an `nn.Parameter`, initialised to `-1.2`, feeding a `torch.distributions.Normal`
- `policy_head` weights and bias zero-initialised, then the throttle bias nudged to `+0.5` so the
  car moves at step zero instead of learning to press the accelerator from scratch

That last detail is the kind of thing a library hides. Here it is three lines of `nn.init` and a
`with torch.no_grad()` block, which is the argument for writing it by hand at all.

The training loop uses the clipped surrogate objective, GAE advantages, an entropy bonus
(`entropy_coef=3e-3`) and **target-KL early stopping** (`target_kl=0.03`) — the whole update is
plain tensor code, no `torch.compile`, no AMP, no distributed anything.

## Checkpoints and a real migration problem

Six `.pt` checkpoints (~0.9 MB each) are committed. `rl_agent.py` carries a **shape-tolerant loader**
that maps an older `backbone.*` state dict onto the current split `actor`/`critic` trunks — evidence
that the architecture changed mid-project and old runs had to keep loading. It is the only piece of
version-migration code in the repo.

## Dependency hygiene

Both `requirements.txt` files pin torch **plus its entire transitive tree** — `filelock`, `fsspec`,
`Jinja2`, `MarkupSafe`, `mpmath`, `networkx`, `sympy`, `typing_extensions`, `numpy` — with identical
versions and differing only in the header comment. That is the signature of `pip freeze`, not of a
curated manifest. There is no `pyproject.toml`, no lockfile and no CI.

⚠ The `a.bhuiyan/requirements.txt` header comments matplotlib as "optional — only needed to plot the
generated racing line", but **matplotlib is not in the list**, while `racing_line.py` imports it for
that plot. See [[documentation-drift]].

## No GPU story

Nothing in the repo records a device, a CUDA version or a training wall-clock. Networks are two
256-unit MLPs, so CPU training is entirely plausible, but the repo does not say — and the throughput
claims that do exist belong to the `parallel` branch, which ships no code here. See
[[branch-per-experiment]].
